title: Finite pushforward preserves punctual upper bounds and purity
statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type schemes over a finite field, and let $\mathcal G$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$. If every local Frobenius eigenvalue of $\mathcal G$ at every closed point has weight at most $w$, then the same holds for $f_{0*}\mathcal G$. If $\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then $f_{0*}\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$.
Here finite morphism, constructibility, Weil sheaves, and direct image use [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-constructible-heart], [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and [def-weil-derived-direct-image], with weights as in [def-weil-punctual-weights].

proof.text: A finite morphism is separated, locally quasi-finite, locally finite type, quasi-compact and proper. The separated structure morphism of Y gives quasi-separatedness. Apply the already-proved native punctual upper-bound theorem recorded in [lem-zl-native-quasi-finite-punctual-weights] to f. The isomorphism lowerStarIsoHigherLowerShriekZero f F, obtained by proper coincidence [lem-sf-native-weil-proper-shriek-star] and degree-zero derived direct image, embeds f_*F into R⁰f!F. HasWeightsAtMost.of_mono transports the bound along its hom.

For purity apply the already-proved source IsPunctuallyPureOfWeight.lowerStar_of_isFinite. Its proof uses exactly the purity calculation of [lem-zl-native-quasi-finite-punctual-weights] and the same proper comparison [lem-sf-native-weil-proper-shriek-star], transporting purity along the isomorphism hom by IsPunctuallyPureOfWeight.of_mono. Pair the two independent implications. No etaleness or nonempty-fibre hypothesis is required.
